Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

forestmap 0.2.1

  • study_ticks = FALSE removes the tick marks and rank numbers from the study axis.
  • New article, “Large meta-analyses”, shows a plot of 250 effects and the settings that keep it readable.
  • The package’s title is now “Visualising Multiple Sources of Meta-Analytic Heterogeneity”, matching its citation.

forestmap 0.2.0

  • Numeric moderators (e.g. mean age) are shown as a single continuous row, drawn as a bar (the default), a tint of the study’s colour, or a grey shade with a coloured stripe (continuous_style). continuous_range adds the range of values to the row’s label, at the end of the row, or as a legend.
  • orientation = "vertical" turns the plot on its side: one study per row, with study names (study) and the heatmap as columns on the right. Suits long meta-analyses.
  • label_size sets the size of study names, level labels and moderator names separately, and level_angle the angle of the vertical layout’s level labels, so crowded labels can be made to fit.
  • With more than 60 studies, points, interval lines and heatmap borders get thinner so neighbouring studies don’t merge.
  • The forest plot now lines up exactly with the heatmap’s columns.
  • citation("forestmap") and CITATION.cff give a citation for the package.

forestmap 0.1.0

  • First version. plot_forestmap() draws a forest plot of the studies in a meta-analysis, sorted by effect size, above a heatmap of study properties. Give each study’s uncertainty as a sampling variance (vi), a standard error (se) or 95% CI bounds (lb, ub). Options: standard and compact layouts; built-in ("default", "okabe_ito", "viridis", "greyscale") and custom palettes; a bundled default font (Roboto Condensed) and custom fonts; automatic or manual panel heights (forest_height); max_levels to merge rare levels into “Other”; rope, null_value and y_limits.
